summary: All six findings accepted as valid scope/clarity corrections; no blocker. Remediation order: (1) R-002+R-005 scope the dependency pre-dispatch gate and freshness predicate out of this version; (2) R-003 scope legacy adoption out and keep read-only discovery; (3) R-001 make the derived catalog index non-mandatory and never a read source; (4) R-004 drop the six-step durability/unknown-commit protocol from design and rely on AtomicWrite plus torn-journal detection; (5) R-006 document the exit-code contract and envelope fields in §14. Minimal targeted edits only; every do_not_change item preserved.

decisions.reason: Correct. The original task requires only viewing tasks; it has no volume or performance requirement. The spec mandated a derived catalog index with cache/rebuild semantics while all read commands derive from journals, so the index was a write-only artifact with durability obligations and no reader.
decisions.evidence: original-task.md lists only catalog scope, local-only data, planned tasks and read commands. Implementation confirms the read path rebuilds from journals (cli/internal/repository/catalog.go Catalog) and the index is never read back.
decisions.resolution: §16 rewritten: read commands derive from authoritative journals; catalog/index.json is not a mandatory artifact, is never a read source, and its absence or corruption does not affect reads. Design 'Команды и read model' updated to match.

decisions.reason: Correct. The original task names dependencies only as a planned-task v1 metadata field. §7 converted that into a controller-owned pre-dispatch execution gate that changes runner behavior and cannot be exercised until the native controller capability exists.
decisions.evidence: original-task.md: 'planned-задача первой версии содержит title, description, priority, labels и dependencies' with no execution semantics. commands.go activate returns BF_BLOCKED in this milestone.
decisions.resolution: §7 rewritten: depends_on stays metadata; pre-dispatch gate, effective-completed/stale classification and attempt binding are explicitly deferred to the native controller write-slice specification; run does not use depends_on in this version. Design 'Dependencies' updated accordingly.

decisions.reason: Correct. The original task does not request legacy migration. The full adoption machinery (portable artifact manifest, immutable segment, lineage receipts, routing manifest) exceeds scope and its apply path is staged unimplemented; read-only discovery alone prevents data loss.
decisions.evidence: original-task.md has no migration requirement. commands.go commandAdopt returns BF_BLOCKED for --apply; main.go help marks adopt --apply as staged BLOCKED.
decisions.resolution: §17/§18 scoped to read-only legacy discovery, fail-closed UUID conflict and bytes preservation; adoption deferred to a separate specification and adopt performs no canonical-store write. Design renamed 'Legacy discovery' and adoption detail removed.

decisions.reason: Correct. The design's explicit six-step durability protocol with commit_outcome=unknown reconciliation describes a crash scenario the task never raises, while AtomicWrite already performs write/fsync/rename/directory-sync and torn journals are surfaced by §15.
decisions.evidence: storage.go AtomicWrite implements atomic publish with file fsync and directory sync; original-task.md contains no crash-durability requirement.
decisions.resolution: Design 'Concurrency и recovery' rewritten to rely on the existing AtomicWrite primitive and torn/conflicting-journal detection; the unknown-commit reconciliation protocol and unknown-temp retention are removed.

decisions.reason: Correct. 'Fresh effective completed' and 'stale-completed' were used as acceptance-relevant predicates with no observable definition, so the dispatch criterion was not objectively implementable. This is resolved together with its only in-scope consumer (R-002).
decisions.evidence: §7 and §18 used the terms without a predicate; the original task does not require dispatch gating at all.
decisions.resolution: §7 drops fresh-effective-completed/stale-completed as undefined for this version; §18 now defines the only retained notion as an observable diagnostic: a record that references an absolute live input that no longer exists is marked stale|orphaned, without changing historical status or acting as a gate.

decisions.reason: Correct. §14 claimed documented exit contracts and the verification section claimed closed schemas, but neither the numeric exit codes nor the read/write envelope field shapes appeared in the specification body.
decisions.evidence: Exit codes existed only in code (commands.go writeError: BF_INVALID=2, otherwise 11); §14 contained no schema or exit table.
decisions.resolution: §14 now fixes schema_version=1, lists write-command and read-command envelope fields, and documents the exit-code contract 0/2/11 with the BF_INVALID/BF_BLOCKED/BF_CONFLICT classes.

do_not_change_checks.item: §1 — resolving a single clone-local store from the verified git common dir shared by all worktrees is the correct, directly required mechanism for the whole-repo/worktree scope.
do_not_change_checks.reason: The original task requires a catalog covering the whole repository and all worktrees; the common-dir store remains the directly required mechanism.
do_not_change_checks.evidence: §1 unchanged; design 'Repository и worktree boundary' still resolves the store from the verified git common dir with clone_id identity.

do_not_change_checks.item: §2 — keeping the immutable hash-linked journal as the single source of truth and making catalog/overview/index derived data that cannot authorize execution/acceptance preserves the existing architecture and recovery semantics.
do_not_change_checks.reason: The R-001 revision keeps journals authoritative and explicitly makes the index non-authoritative, strengthening this principle rather than weakening it.
do_not_change_checks.evidence: §2 and §23 unchanged; revised §16 states read commands derive from authoritative journals and the index is never a read source.

do_not_change_checks.item: §3 — the planned-task v1 field set (title/description/priority/labels/depends_on) and the explicit exclusions (milestones, assignee, comments, due dates, custom fields) are correct minimal scoping.
do_not_change_checks.reason: The field set and exclusions match the original task and were not touched by any accepted finding.
do_not_change_checks.evidence: §3 and the 'Не делать' section are unchanged; §7 edits concern execution semantics, not the field set.

do_not_change_checks.item: §6 — treating archived as a presentation flag that never alters next_action/acceptance/recovery/dependency result is correct and prevents a subtle execution-status bug.
do_not_change_checks.reason: Archive-as-presentation-flag remains correct and is independent of the reverted dependency-gate scope.
do_not_change_checks.evidence: §6 unchanged; tests assert archiving preserves lifecycle (repository_test.go TestArchiveAndUnarchiveArePresentationFlags).

do_not_change_checks.item: §15 — corrupt/torn/conflicting journals must surface as diagnostic entries without hiding other tasks; this is a correct robustness requirement.
do_not_change_checks.reason: Corrupt-journal diagnostics remain a required robustness property and are now also the mechanism that replaces the removed unknown-commit protocol.
do_not_change_checks.evidence: §15 unchanged; revised design 'Concurrency и recovery' explicitly relies on torn/conflicting-journal detection; TestCorruptTaskIsDiagnosticNotFatal covers it.

do_not_change_checks.item: §19 + design 'Security и privacy' — redacting prompts/evidence/credentials from list/overview and using allowlisted projections is justified because existing controller journals store raw prompts and evidence.
do_not_change_checks.reason: Redaction remains necessary because legacy journals contain raw prompts/evidence, independent of the adoption scope reduction.
do_not_change_checks.evidence: §19 unchanged; legacy.go reads request.prompt only to derive a safe display title; list/show project allowlisted fields.

do_not_change_checks.item: 'Не делать' section — no Markdown-per-task storage, no SQL/daemon/second database, no tasks.md, no automatic deletion of completed tasks, no automatic dependency execution; these correctly constrain scope.
do_not_change_checks.reason: All non-goals still hold; deferring the dependency gate and adoption is consistent with 'no automatic dependency execution' and no second database.
do_not_change_checks.evidence: 'Не делать' section unchanged; no accepted finding required altering it.
